children: Washington delivered another packed round of headlines, from a reported
database intrusion to fresh fights over Social Security, health care and Senate leadership. Here’s a quick recap of the major political stories that stood out over the week.
Trump Links FBI Database Hack to Voter Fraud Claims

said Saturday that an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center could have an unexpected upside, potentially exposing information tied to alleged voter fraud. The intrusion marks the second reported breach involving the bureau’s systems in recent years. Details remained limited, but the incident placed the FBI’s sensitive criminal-information database under renewed scrutiny.
Cassidy Says Trump Supports $1.5 Trillion Social Security Plan
(R-La.) said a proposed $1.5 trillion investment fund could satisfy as much as 70% of Social Security’s financing needs, warning that lawmakers’ failure to act threatens the program. On
“Face the Nation,” he said Trump supported the proposal and cited commitments from Senate Majority Leader
(R-Idaho) to schedule a hearing and markup.
Biden Criticizes Trump’s White House Ballroom Project

criticized Trump over the demolition of the White House’s East Wing to create a ballroom reportedly costing $600 million. Biden objected to the scale and symbolism of the construction, calling it “beneath the country” and an attempt to create monuments to himself. The gold-heavy design also drew his attention.
Van Hollen Challenges Schumer for Senate Democratic Leadership

(D-N.Y.) for Senate Democratic leader in a caucus vote scheduled for Dec. 1. Speaking on “The MeidasTouch Podcast,” he presented himself as an underdog while arguing the race remains unsettled, saying, “this is a wide-open race.”
Sanders Renews Medicare for All Campaign
(I-Vt.) renewed his call for Medicare for All after former President
acknowledged limitations in the Affordable Care Act. Sanders shared a clip Saturday of Obama speaking at a meeting organized by House Minority Leader
(D-N.Y.), arguing that restoring the existing law would not go far enough. His message: “Restoring Obamacare Alone Is Not the Answer.”

title: Biden Criticizes White House Ballroom Project, Trump Sees Upside in FBI Hack and More: This Week in Politics
